# Vardath Cosmology: The World That Opens

## Stephen Michael Hawton / Vardath

---

# Preface — Why I Am Writing This

I did not begin with a cosmology.

I began with a question about a serpent.

That matters to me because Vardath Cosmology was never one complete picture that arrived all at once. It grew by following one idea into another until the pieces stopped looking like separate curiosities and began behaving like parts of the same world.

At first there was the serpent: something long, moving and powerful enough to shape land and water. Then came the figure in the current, the possibility that a large energetic structure could look human from one angle and geometric from another. Then came the axis, the enclosure, the world above and below, the paired winding channels, the gate, the woven field, the upper water, the carrier and finally the idea that the world itself might be one turn of a much larger living structure.

Some of those early pictures changed almost beyond recognition.

That is part of the story.

I do not want to write this book as though I sat down one morning with the finished model already in my head. I did not. I followed it. Sometimes one branch opened into another. Sometimes an image that first looked literal also became useful as a viewpoint. Sometimes an object I thought was one thing turned out to fit inside a larger structure without losing the earlier possibility.

The world-machine became clearer every time I stopped forcing the symbols to be objects and began asking what job they were doing.

A serpent could be a current.

A tree could be an axis.

A wheel could be an end-on view of a node.

A mountain could be the landscape image of convergence.

An ark could be a small protected world.

A god could be an operator rather than the apparatus itself.

A flood could be a consequence of a boundary change rather than the original cause.

A gate could be a temporary change in what is next to what.

That last idea changed almost everything.

The cosmology I describe in this book is a speculative model of a world that is not isolated, not static and not created once and then left alone. I picture the world we inhabit as one stable turn of a larger growing body. What came before is not simply gone. What comes next is not simply absent. Previous, present and next belong to the same structure.

A persistent current runs through that structure.

A woven lattice organises it.

Most of the time the lattice is broad. The world is quiet in the sense that its deeper architecture is not forcing itself into ordinary experience. Water remains in familiar reservoirs. The atmosphere behaves like the atmosphere of one world. Land is stable enough for geography to mean something. The sky is broad. Neighbouring turns remain separate enough that each behaves like its own environment.

Then the state can change.

The current strengthens or changes mode. The lattice begins to gather. A broad weave narrows. The same structure that looked like mesh can become strip, ladder, rod and finally throat. At maximum convergence, regions that are normally separated can become temporarily adjacent.

That is the gate.

The gate is not a permanent hole in the sky.

It is a phase.

While that phase lasts, water can move. Air can move. Heat and pressure can move. Fine material can move. Rock and sediment can become cargo. Living things can survive inside protected enclosures or cross through active vehicles. The surface can deform while the larger world-body remains continuous.

Then the gate closes.

The lattice widens again.

The worlds separate.

Water settles into new basins. Sediment becomes new ground. The atmosphere finds a new balance. Life expands from what survived. What looked like catastrophe from inside the old arrangement becomes inheritance from the viewpoint of the next one.

That is the current picture.

And behind all of it is the idea that finally made the myths, legends and fairy tales feel like parts of one problem rather than unrelated curiosities.

I think the gate is **a natural door through time**.

Not a machine built by one lost civilisation and not a different magical portal for every culture. One recurring event. One world-structure entering the same kind of state at different times in history. Each appearance is seen from a different place, by different people, through different language and belief.

That is why I expect the record to look fragmented.

One witness remembers a shining road. Another remembers a world tree. Another remembers a fairy mound, an underworld passage, a heavenly ladder, a flood, a mountain opening, a serpent, a rider crossing impossible distance, or a meeting across ages. The stories do not need to agree in detail if they are human memories of the same class of event seen from different positions and at different phases.

This book is my attempt to explain that as one connected cosmology rather than hundreds of separate notes, posts, comparisons and discoveries.

Other branches of my work developed alongside this one, but they are not the subject here.

Here I want to stay with the world itself.

I want to describe the serpent, the lattice, the current, the world-turns, the upper boundary, the gate, the carriers, the moving crust, the waking sky, the reset and the next world. I want to show how those pieces fit together without stopping every few pages to turn the story back into a laboratory notebook.

I also want to explain why mythology became so important to me without pretending mythology proves the model.

That distinction matters.

The Rainbow Serpent belongs to Aboriginal Australian traditions before I compare the serpent with a moving current.

Yggdrasil belongs to Norse tradition before I compare the world tree with a persistent connector among levels.

Revelation is Christian apocalyptic literature before I compare its sequence of opening, celestial disturbance, conflict, deformation and renewal with my world cycle.

Tiamat, Nut, the Duat, Meru, Oceanus, Janus, Jörmungandr and every other figure or structure discussed in this book belong to their own histories first.

My reading comes afterward.

I am not trying to prove that every culture secretly had one religion or one hidden technical manual.

I am asking a different question.

What happens if the physical structure of my cosmology is stated first, and then mythology is read by **role, relation and viewpoint**?

That approach changed the comparative work completely.

A tree is not automatically the same thing as a mountain.

A mountain is not automatically the same thing as a pillar.

A pillar is not automatically the same thing as a rod.

But all of them can occupy the axial family.

An eye is not a wheel.

A wheel is not a star.

A star is not a rosette.

But all of them can be produced by radial geometry viewed end-on.

A serpent wrapped around the world is not the same as two serpents around a staff.

A dragon guarding a threshold is not the same as a current moving through the land.

But all of them can belong to the wider serpent family at different scales and phases.

Once I began thinking like that, the myths became less like a box of clues and more like different camera angles.

That is how I want them treated in this book.

The strongest comparisons are not the ones where one symbol happens to resemble another.

The strongest are the ones where several relationships stay in the same order.

A boundary is closed.

Something activates it.

A route opens.

A traveller or carrier crosses.

Water or fire accompanies the transition.

The old arrangement changes or breaks open.

A remnant survives.

The world becomes stable again.

That is much more useful to me than a single shared serpent or tree, because the relationships begin to accumulate into a larger pattern.

I still treat that pattern as something to explore and integrate rather than as a final proof.

The cosmology has to stand as a cosmology.

That means I also need to leave the speculative parts visible.

The upper ocean is a proposal.

The exact physical nature of the deep current is unresolved.

The support conditions of the world boundary are unresolved.

The way the sky would be organised by the lattice is unresolved.

The scale and energy of a world-level contraction are unresolved.

The biological consequences of a waking atmosphere are even more speculative.

I am comfortable saying that.

I would rather have a growing model with open edges than close those edges too early and lose possibilities that may later connect.

The book therefore speaks in two voices that are really one voice used carefully.

When I describe **what Vardath Cosmology proposes**, I will explain it directly.

When I reach a place where the physical mechanism is still uncertain, I will say so.

I do not need to apologise for the model being speculative.

That is what it is.

The value, for me, lies in whether the pieces can be integrated into a coherent structure and whether that structure gives me a stronger way to understand the repeated images and relationships that first drew me into the problem.

The most important change in my thinking was learning to see catastrophe as transition.

A flood is terrifying if you stand inside the old world.

A gate is dangerous if you are exposed when the boundary opens.

A moving crust destroys familiar geography.

A waking sky can look like the end of everything.

But from the viewpoint of the larger world-body, those events can also be the mechanism by which continuity moves forward.

The old world gives material to the next.

Water is redistributed.

Life survives inside smaller enclosures.

The next world receives inheritance.

The system opens, transfers and closes.

The catastrophe is real.

So is the continuity.

That is why the cosmology keeps returning to eggs, shells, caves, baskets, arks, wombs and trees.

They are all different ways of solving the same problem:

**how can an inside remain coherent while the outside changes?**

The world itself may be the largest version of that enclosure.

A stable world is an inside.

A gate event disturbs its boundary.

A carrier creates a smaller inside within the unstable larger one.

The renewed world creates a new stable inside afterward.

The pattern repeats across scale.

The same is true of the world tree.

At first I thought mainly in terms of a tree connecting levels.

Later I began to think of the tree as a woven structure through time as well as space. If previous, present and next are neighbouring turns of one larger body, then the tree is not simply a ladder between places. It can become a connector between states of the world itself.

That is where Yggdrasil became more than a mythic parallel for me.

It became a way of thinking about the door.

Not a door that takes someone to a distant planet, but a door that temporarily changes which world-state is adjacent to which.

Past, present and future become a physical relationship inside the larger structure.

That idea belongs later in the book because it only makes sense once the gate has been built carefully.

I mention it here because it captures the direction the whole project has taken.

I began by asking what the serpent was doing.

I ended up asking what the world is doing.

The answer I have built is that the world is growing, breathing, separating, approaching, exchanging and settling.

The ordinary world is one phase of that process.

The great event is another.

Myth, in my reading, is what the event looks like when remembered from inside.

This book is my attempt to put that complete picture in one place.

Not as a final answer.

As the clearest version of the world I have been trying to describe.

---

# Introduction — A World That Changes Its Adjacencies

Imagine the ordinary world first.

Not an apocalypse. Not a giant tree filling the sky. Not a serpent of fire, a rolled firmament, a gate between realms or a flood covering the land.

Just the world as it appears now.

Land is land. Oceans have coastlines. The atmosphere circulates. The sky is broad. The Sun, Moon, planets and stars follow the regular motions we have learned to expect. A mountain stays where it was yesterday. Rivers still know which way is downhill.

That is where Vardath Cosmology begins.

At the centre of the model is one further idea that runs through this entire book: **the great gate is a natural door through time**.

I do not picture history as containing hundreds of unrelated supernatural portals. I picture one class of natural world-event recurring at different times. When the larger structure enters the gate-state, normally separated world-states can become temporarily adjacent. People living in different ages encounter the same underlying event from different places, cultures and stages of the cycle.

That is why the record is scattered.

One age remembers a world tree. Another remembers a fairy road, hollow hill or impossible journey. Another remembers a flood, a bridge, a mountain opening, a shining wheel, a serpent, a descent into an underworld, a visit to another realm, a meeting with someone who should belong to another time, or a land that seems to have moved from where history says it should be.

In my cosmology these are not automatically separate phenomena. They can be different human records of the same natural door appearing again and again through history.

I call the ordinary condition the **quiet world**.

Quiet does not mean motionless.

Everything can be moving and the world can still be quiet in the sense I mean. Weather moves. Water moves. Crust moves. Life grows. The sky changes hour by hour. The deeper current proposed by the model can also remain active.

Quiet means the larger structure is not forcing neighbouring world-states into contact.

The present world is stable enough to behave like one world.

That distinction is the foundation of everything that follows.

## One world inside a larger body

In Vardath Cosmology, the world we inhabit is not the entire structure.

It is one stabilised turn of something larger.

Behind or beneath it is an older turn: the previous world-state retained inside the larger growth.

Beyond or above it is another populated turn: a world-state that is next relative to us, but already a world in its own right within the same body.

I use words like *above* and *below* because the model is layered, but the relation is also temporal.

The older turn is the inherited past.

The present turn is the world-state we currently inhabit.

The next turn is the populated world that is future-relative to us.

They are not three unrelated universes.

They are successive parts of one continuing structure.

One point needs to be explicit here: **all of these world-turns are populated**.

Previous, present and next do not mean dead world, inhabited world and unborn world.

They describe the worlds' relationship to the world I am standing in.

A world above or below can have its own inhabitants, ecology, history and stable order while remaining separated from us. The gate changes adjacency between populated worlds. It does not populate an empty one.

The closest ordinary image is a growing shell.

A shell keeps its earlier turns while adding new ones. The older material does not vanish merely because growth continues. The new turn develops in continuity with what came before.

That is the broad relation I am proposing.

The model does not require everyday geography to stop being geography. A city still has a location on the present surface. A road still goes from one place to another. A river still follows the terrain.

The larger world-body adds another kind of relationship: how the present surface sits among the neighbouring turns and what happens when those normally separated regions begin to approach one another.

That is where the lattice enters.

## The hidden lattice

I use the word **lattice** for the woven structure connecting the larger world-body.

I do not mean a rigid metal cage sitting visibly over the sky.

I mean a connected field of paths, crossings and nodes.

A woven structure can distribute movement.

It can carry tension.

It can contain local junctions.

It can be broad in one state and narrow in another.

That last property became the key.

The mature Vardath model contains paired, counter-wound movement inside the larger weave. One family of paths can have one axial sense while another has the opposite sense.

That is the mechanical descendant of the old paired-serpent image.

The serpent did not survive because I decided every mythic snake was secretly cosmic machinery.

It survived because a serpent is an extraordinarily natural image for a moving line.

Two serpents winding around one centre are an equally natural image for opposed movement organised around a shared axis.

Most of the time, the lattice is broad.

That broad state is the quiet world.

Paths remain distributed.

Local nodes exist without becoming full gates.

The sky remains an extended field instead of collapsing toward one dominant centre.

The neighbouring turns remain effectively separate.

Then the state begins to change.

I call that change **activation**.

## The current and the pulse

The model proposes a persistent deep current.

The exact physical carrier of that current is not settled. I am not pretending I have finished the physics simply because the structural idea is clear to me.

What matters at this stage is the difference between the current and the **pulse**.

The current persists.

The pulse is the active condition in which the current begins driving the world-machine into a different state.

This same distinction appears all through the cosmology.

The lattice exists before it contracts.

The boundary exists before it becomes a gate.

The node exists before it opens.

The world tree exists before it becomes traversable.

The event is therefore not the sudden appearance of a completely foreign mechanism.

It is a state change in something already present.

During activation, local preferred paths strengthen.

Nodes become more important.

The broad structure begins to organise.

Then comes **convergence**.

## From the broad world to the through-route

In the quiet world, direction is spread.

Movement around the surface dominates ordinary experience.

During convergence, more of the structure begins to gather toward an axial route.

This is not a claim that every compass bearing literally collapses into a pole.

It is a change in which geometry dominates.

The stable world is broad.

The active world becomes increasingly axial.

That means the world can move through a continuous visual sequence:

**field → weave → narrow strip → ladder-like form → rod → throat**

The great question was how one structure could pass through those states without becoming a completely different object.

The fingertrap supplied the best answer I have found.

## Why the fingertrap matters

A woven fingertrap is wide in one state and narrow in another.

Pull it along its length and the weave changes angle. The sleeve becomes longer and thinner. Release it and it can broaden again.

The strands remain the same strands.

That simple behaviour gave me a mechanical bridge between symbols that had previously looked unrelated.

The broad lattice did not need to disappear so that a rod could replace it.

The rod could be the lattice under contraction.

The ladder could be an intermediate view of the narrowed weave.

The throat could be the most concentrated state of the same structure.

That changed the cosmology from a collection of objects into a transformation.

A tree, ladder, pillar and rod no longer had to be competing answers to the question of what the world-axis was.

They could be different appearances or states of one family.

A wheel, eye, ring or star could be what a radial node looked like end-on.

A serpent could be one moving strand.

A paired-serpent image could be two opposed strands around the same centre.

The important claim is not that the symbols all historically meant the same thing.

The important claim is that the geometry can generate several of them.

## The gate

At maximum convergence, the throat takes on its most important function.

It changes **adjacency**.

That is the mature definition of the gate.

I do not imagine a permanent portal standing open between worlds.

I imagine normally separated regions becoming temporarily capable of direct exchange because the geometry that kept them apart has changed.

During the quiet state, the previous, present and next turns are effectively separate.

During the gate interval, some part of that separation weakens.

The present world can become connected to a region of the next world above or the previous world below.

The gate therefore does not need to be a doorway installed in the sky.

It is a phase of the structure.

This also explains why it closes naturally.

When the contraction ends, the geometry that created the unusual adjacency ends with it.

The lattice widens.

The throat loses dominance.

The neighbouring turns separate again.

The gate disappears because the world has changed state.

## What crosses

Once the gate exists, the next question is unavoidable.

What crosses it?

Water is the most obvious material because water already belongs to the boundary structure of the cosmology.

The mature model proposes that an upper watery region may be the lower boundary of the already populated next world-turn. From the present world it appears above. From that world's own surface it would be below.

During the quiet phase, the interface is stable.

During activation, it can become part of the transfer.

That gives flood a very different role from ordinary weather.

The flood is no longer the whole explanation.

It is one visible consequence of a boundary becoming active.

Atmosphere can cross as well.

Pressure, vapour and heat become part of the event.

Fine material can be carried.

Sediment can move.

Rock can become debris.

The crust itself can deform while water is moving over it.

Living material can survive if it remains protected or if the crossing conditions allow it.

This is why carriers became so important to the model.

## The enclosure principle

An ark, basket, chest, cave, egg, shell or womb all solve one basic problem.

They create an **inside** that stays coherent while the outside becomes dangerous.

That is the enclosure principle.

The carrier does not have to understand the gate.

Its job is to preserve the cargo.

This can happen while the medium does the moving.

A basket floats.

An ark rides the water.

A cave remains still while the world outside changes.

An egg protects life until it can emerge into another environment.

At world scale, the same logic applies.

The stable world itself is an enclosure.

During a reset, smaller enclosures can preserve continuity while the larger one changes.

That is why so many creation and flood stories became interesting to me.

Not because every one of them proves the cosmology, but because the same functional problem appears again and again:

**how does life cross a world transition without ceasing to be life?**

## The land becomes cargo

The land is not the lattice.

That distinction is essential.

The lattice is the deeper organising structure in the model.

The crust is material riding above it.

I sometimes call the crust **rubble on the lattice** because the phrase keeps the hierarchy clear.

Land can bend, shear, break, rotate, rise, sink and be buried.

The deeper structure can remain continuous while the visible map changes.

This is where the large bends and arcs of the world became interesting to me.

The Americas, the Mediterranean and Africa, Arabia, India, Southeast Asia, Indonesia, New Guinea and eastern Australia all show large curved relationships at different scales.

I do not claim that a single drawn line on a map proves the lattice.

The cosmological idea is simpler.

If the deeper driver contains organised shear and changing directions, the crust above it should not be expected to move only in straight lines.

It can bend.

Water then outlines the new relief.

The final coastline becomes the combined result of land deformation and where the redistributed water settles.

## The sky is also part of the machine

The same principle applies upward.

The sky is not empty background in Vardath Cosmology.

It is part of the larger structure.

That does not mean I have solved the exact physical nature of the Sun, Moon, planets and stars inside the model.

I have not.

The stronger claim is architectural.

The celestial field belongs to the same changing geometry as the gate.

During the quiet phase, the field is broad and ordinary.

During activation, nodes can become more prominent.

During convergence, the sky can become increasingly organised around the axial structure.

At maximum contraction, the broad field can be dominated by what I call the **rod-body**.

During reopening, the field spreads again and the ordinary-looking sky returns.

This is one reason myths containing eyes, wheels, stars, rods and radiant figures can sit so close together in the Vardath reading.

They may be different visual responses to an active geometry.

Again, that is a comparison, not proof.

## Mythology comes after the machine

Only after the physical structure is stated do I want to compare mythology.

That order matters.

The myths are not allowed to decide freely what the cosmology should become every time a new symbol appears.

The model first defines roles.

Then I ask where those roles appear elsewhere.

The main roles include:

- **axis** — the central connecting geometry;
- **gate** — the temporary state of changed adjacency;
- **operator** — a figure associated with directing, ordering or activating the event;
- **vehicle** — an active means of crossing;
- **carrier** — an enclosure that preserves cargo;
- **guide** — one who knows the route;
- **guardian** — one who controls or marks the threshold;
- **manifestation** — the visible form of the active structure;
- **medium** — water, wind, cloud, fire, radiance or current surrounding the transition;
- **witness** — the observer who experiences only one view of the event;
- **reset** — the reorganisation that turns catastrophe into a successor world.

Different traditions can preserve different roles.

One may be dominated by the tree.

Another by the flood.

Another by a guarded bridge.

Another by a world-serpent.

Another by a rolled sky.

Another by a child carried through water.

Another by an old body becoming the material of a new cosmos.

They do not need to be the same story to become structurally interesting beside one another.

That is the approach I take throughout the book.

## Reopening

The gate cannot stay open.

If it did, the worlds would not regain separate environments.

The event ends by reversing the contraction.

The throat loses dominance.

The braid widens.

Nodes close.

Water and atmosphere settle.

Sediment is deposited.

The land retains the scars of movement.

Life emerges from protected pockets and surviving lineages.

The next stable state begins.

This is where the word **reset** can be misleading.

I do not mean rewind.

The world does not return to the exact arrangement it had before.

A reset in Vardath Cosmology is a **handoff**.

The new world inherits material and life from what came before while settling into a different arrangement.

The world survives by changing.

## The full cycle

The complete movement can be written simply:

**quiet world → activation → convergence → throat → changed adjacency → transfer → deformation and reset → reopening → renewed quiet world**

That is the central machine of this book.

Everything else grows around it.

The serpent is the moving line.

The lattice is the broad connected form.

The fingertrap explains contraction.

The rod is the concentrated state.

The gate is the temporary contact.

Water, atmosphere and land reveal the consequences.

The carrier preserves continuity.

The world tree holds the long connection.

The myths give us different human views of the event.

And the renewed world becomes quiet enough that the event itself can fade into memory.

Vardath Cosmology is therefore not fundamentally a story about the end of the world.

It is a story about **how one world can become the next without the larger world-body losing continuity**.

# Part I — Finding the Hidden Shape

# Chapter 1 — The Serpent and the Question

The oldest recoverable part of Vardath Cosmology is not the shell.

It is not the lattice.

It is not the shell, the upper ocean, the layered worlds or the finger-trap rod.

It is the Rainbow Serpent.

That fact matters to me because it reveals what I was looking for before I knew what the later model would become.

I was not originally trying to build a geometry of neighbouring worlds.

I was trying to understand a moving thing.

## A necessary boundary

Before I describe the Vardath interpretation, I need to separate it from the traditions that inspired the question.

Rainbow Serpent traditions belong to Aboriginal Australian peoples and vary across Country, language groups and communities. There is no single universal pan-Australian Rainbow Serpent doctrine that can simply be lifted out of Indigenous religion and turned into my cosmology.

Publicly described traditions can associate Rainbow Serpent beings with creation, waterholes, rock passages, rivers, seasonal processes, law, life and the shaping of Country. Those meanings belong to the source traditions.

The plasma/current interpretation is mine.

That distinction remains important throughout this book.

I am interested in what happens when a traditional form is placed beside a modern speculative mechanical question. I am not claiming that the modern mechanism is the hidden “real meaning” of the tradition.

With that boundary stated, the reason the Rainbow Serpent became the beginning of the project is simple:

it already behaves like a **line that moves through the world**.

## From creature to path

A creature is usually imagined as an object occupying a place.

A serpent suggests something different.

Its identity is inseparable from its path.

It curves.

It coils.

Its body is a record of movement.

A long serpent across a landscape can resemble a river, fault, ridge, lightning channel, filament or current without any of those things literally being an animal.

The geometry itself invites translation.

That became the first Vardath move.

Instead of asking only:

**What being is the Rainbow Serpent?**

I began asking:

**What physical process would leave a serpent-like path while changing water and land?**

That question transformed the image.

The serpent could now be read as a moving current.

Not a static cosmic snake hanging in the sky, but an energetic channel whose path matters.

The world around the line responds.

Water collects, releases or changes route.

Ground can be cut, raised or reorganised.

Storm, radiance and colour can belong to the same energetic episode.

What later became the deep lattice is already present here in embryo.

The serpent is one strand before I knew there was a weave.

## The earliest event grammar

The early Rainbow Serpent branch already contained a sequence that would survive almost everything that came later:

> **stable world → energetic activation → serpentine manifestation → interaction with water and land → retreat or release → changed equilibrium**

At the time, I did not have the mature vocabulary.

There was no formal distinction between current and pulse.

There was no previous/present/next world-turn.

There was no gate defined as changed adjacency.

There was no finger-trap mechanism.

But the event was already dynamic.

That is crucial.

The cosmology did not begin with a picture of a world.

It began with a picture of a world **being acted upon**.

This may be why the later project became so resistant to static cosmologies.

Whenever I found a structure—a tree, mountain, rod, wheel, shell or grid—the question quickly became:

**What does it do when the world changes state?**

The serpent had trained the project to think in verbs.

## The Sun-biting branch

One early retelling pushed the idea into a more dramatic form.

The Serpent interacted with a plasma-like Sun, provoking a dangerous energetic response. Wind and water were involved in restoring a safer condition.

I keep that story as one possible celestial reading rather than locking it into one final mechanism.

The physical nature of the Sun, Moon and planets remains open in the cosmology, which means the Sun-biting branch can sit beside later celestial ideas instead of having to be thrown away.

What it adds most strongly is **contact**.

It introduced **contact**.

A moving serpentine current was no longer only shaping passive landscape. It could encounter another energetic structure. The encounter could change heat, light, wind and water.

That later became a general rule:

> **catastrophic visible effects may be consequences of changing relationships between larger structures, not independent disasters.**

The “bite” can therefore be understood as an early narrative form of coupling.

That way of thinking later became much more precise when I started using the language of adjacency.

## Why the serpent kept expanding into new roles

Many early ideas changed scale, role or relationship as the cosmology grew.

The serpent kept expanding with them.

That is not because serpent mythology is rare or uniquely mysterious. It is not.

Serpents are extremely common symbolic forms for ordinary reasons: real snakes are visually striking, dangerous, sinuous, renewing through skin-shedding, associated with ground and water, and easy to translate into narrative.

A serpent image becomes most useful to me when it joins other relationships—water, land-shaping, enclosure, axis, current or boundary.

What made the serpent especially valuable inside the model was not frequency alone.

It was **mechanical flexibility**.

The same strand can occupy different roles depending on state.

### Serpent as creator current

In the earliest branch, the serpent moves through Country and helps form landscape.

Mechanically, this corresponds to an organising current.

### Serpent as obstruction

In the Vṛtra comparison, the serpent or dragon is associated with blocked or confined waters until a violent activation releases them.

Mechanically, this corresponds to a constrained channel or boundary condition.

### Serpent as controlled channel

In caduceus-like imagery, paired serpents wind around one axis.

Mechanically, this corresponds to two coupled opposed paths.

### Serpent as boundary

In some world-serpent traditions, the serpent is circumferential.

Mechanically, this suggests containment or a boundary state.

### Serpent as active dragon

In catastrophe traditions, a serpent or dragon becomes an opponent during breakdown.

Mechanically, this can represent an unstable or conflicting current relation.

The moral meaning changes.

The geometry does not need to.

That distinction became one of the central habits of the mature mythology work.

A recurring shape can be ancestor in one tradition, enemy in another, guardian in another and vehicle of order in another if the cultures are remembering or symbolising different roles.

## From one line to two

The next important step was duplication.

One serpent is a path.

Two serpents can form a braid.

That transition changed the whole project.

A pair introduces polarity.

The strands can wind in the same sense or opposite senses.

They can cross.

They can define an axis between them.

They can create repeated local openings.

They can be imagined as carrying opposite flows.

This is where the later caduceus connection became mechanically useful.

The familiar staff-and-serpents image should not be treated as proof of the Vardath world-machine.

Its value is conceptual.

It compresses three things into one diagram:

1. a central axis;
2. two winding channels;
3. a repeating relationship between those channels.

The mature braid eventually turned that image from symbol into an explicit kinematic construction.

Schematically, two strands can be represented so that their axial terms differ in sign:

> **z_A = pθ + a sin(kθ)**  
> **z_B = pθ − a sin(kθ)**

The exact equations are a model, not a measured cosmic structure.

Their importance is that they show something the early serpent intuition needed:

**one coupled braid can contain simultaneous opposed axial motion.**

The serpent is no longer only a line moving forward.

It becomes part of circulation.

## The current beneath the world

The mature model now separates the **persistent current** from the spectacular serpent manifestation.

That is a major refinement.

The current is proposed to remain part of the world-body even during the quiet phase.

It is not created every time a catastrophe begins.

A stronger pulse makes more of the structure visible or active.

In that sense the serpent can be understood as a manifestation of the current under particular conditions rather than the permanent appearance of the current itself.

This solves a recurrence problem inside the model.

If each reset required a completely new cosmic current to arrive from nowhere, the theory would need a separate origin story for every event.

If one persistent current remains embedded in the world structure, later events can be changes in state of the same system.

The cycle becomes:

> **persistent current → stronger pulse → visible/active current geometry → relaxation → persistent current**

That pattern later repeats at every level.

A boundary becomes a gate and returns to a boundary.

A node opens and closes.

A broad lattice contracts and reopens.

A sleeping god wakes and sleeps.

The current is the first example of this deeper principle:

**state changes matter more than object replacement.**

## The serpent and the land

The early Serpent branch also established another idea that would later reappear in the geological model:

the deep structure does not merely produce images in the sky.

It can move the world below.

That is a much stronger claim than symbolic resemblance.

If a real current-lattice shapes land, there should eventually be measurable physical consequences.

The modern geological extension describes the crust as a **rubble layer** riding on or within a deeper organiser.

The phrase is intentionally crude.

It prevents the model from confusing visible geography with the persistent lattice.

Land can break while the deeper structure survives.

Continents can move while the larger pattern remains.

Mountains can be pushed up where material jams.

Rifts can form where material is pulled apart.

Curved island arcs can reflect redirected motion.

The S-shaped continental intuition came from this branch.

If neighbouring deeper cells produce alternating senses of shear, transported surface material can curve one way and then the other.

That suggests broad S-forms rather than simple radial motion.

But the standard for that idea is much higher than visual resemblance.

Plate tectonics already describes and measures plate motions quantitatively.

A deeper Vardath driver would have to reproduce the real vectors, ridges, faults, subduction zones, trenches and mountain systems with one fixed field.

If the hidden lattice must be redrawn after every mismatch, it explains nothing.

This is the difference between the earliest serpent intuition and the mature geological burden.

The intuition says:

**a moving line shapes land.**

The mature question asks:

**what single field equation would make the measured crust do what it actually does?**

The book will return to that problem much later.

For now, the important point is historical.

The land was never an afterthought.

From the beginning, the serpent was interesting because it moved matter.

## Water is not one symbol

The serpent also forced me to become more careful about water.

Early comparative work can become useless very quickly if every occurrence of water is counted as the same motif.

Water can be:

- a primordial medium;
- an upper boundary;
- a lower hidden domain;
- an ocean separating regions;
- a flood;
- a river route;
- a carrier medium;
- a life source;
- a released reservoir;
- a receiving environment.

The serpent-water relationship only becomes informative when the role is specified.

That is why Vṛtra is more useful than a random snake beside a river.

The sequence contains a relationship:

> **obstruction → violent activation → release of waters**

Likewise, the Rainbow Serpent comparison is stronger when the moving current and landscape-water formation are related.

The mature model makes water a tracer.

Water responds to geometry.

If the gate changes adjacency or pressure, water moves.

If the lattice deforms the surface, water finds new gradients.

If an enclosure holds, water becomes transport rather than direct threat.

The serpent branch therefore taught the project to ask not only **where water appears**, but **what the water is doing**.

## The first world-forming current

At its most expansive, the current hypothesis eventually became a creation model.

A primordial Birkeland-like or filamentary current passes through an undifferentiated world-condition.

Stable regions form around or along it.

Matter accumulates.

Water occupies boundaries and basins.

Atmosphere fills stable chambers.

Life develops later inside the environment organised around the older structure.

This is one of the boldest extensions in Vardath Cosmology.

It is also one of the least physically derived.

The assistant notes on the website correctly separate it from established plasma physics. Anthony Peratt's Z-pinch work can supply a visual vocabulary for pinched high-current forms; it does not establish a nine-chamber world-body or the Vardath creation sequence.

The physical theory would have to answer basic questions.

What carries the current?

Where does the circuit close?

What maintains it over the proposed timescale?

What field strengths are involved?

Why would stable large-scale chambers form?

How does that structure divide into the world-regions later imagined around Yggdrasil?

How do matter, water and atmosphere become organised around the current?

Those questions remain open.

But the role of the idea in the cosmology is clear.

It makes the serpent/current older than the visible world.

The world becomes something that grows around a process.

That is a very different cosmological intuition from imagining matter first and current later.

## The first hidden skeleton

This is the point where the earliest Rainbow Serpent idea connects directly to the current model.

The mature world has a hidden skeleton.

In the quiet phase, the skeleton is not obvious.

The surface world dominates perception.

Land, water, atmosphere and ordinary celestial motion appear self-contained.

During activation, the deeper structure expresses itself more strongly.

The serpent returns.

Not necessarily as a literal enormous snake.

As motion.

As a path.

As a current.

As a pattern of convergence.

As a change in what the world allows to touch.

The serpent is therefore the oldest image in the project and one of the least literal in the mature model.

It is the first name I gave to the idea that the world contains a moving line deeper than the landscape.

## From serpent to question

The most important contribution of the Rainbow Serpent branch was not an answer.

It was a better question.

At the beginning, I could have spent the whole project asking whether different cultures contained serpent gods.

That would have produced an endless catalogue and very little cosmology.

Instead, the serpent made the project ask:

> **What kind of underlying process could repeatedly become serpent, current, channel, obstruction, boundary, braid and dragon depending on state and viewpoint?**

That question led to the axis.

The axis led to perspective.

Perspective led to Squatter Man.

Squatter Man led to the possibility that a current could look human.

The human form led to trees, crosses, mountains, staffs and hanging figures.

Those images led to an enclosure.

The enclosure led to paired channels.

The paired channels led to polarity.

Polarity eventually became the counter-wound braid.

The braid met the finger trap.

The finger trap finally turned the broad sky and narrow rod into two states of one structure.

So when I say Vardath Cosmology began with the Rainbow Serpent, I do not mean that the entire cosmology is an interpretation of Aboriginal tradition.

I mean the first durable conceptual move came from taking a winding creator form seriously as **geometry in motion**.

The serpent was the first line.

Everything else was the attempt to discover what that line belonged to.

---

# Chapter 2 — The Figure in the Current

The serpent gave me a moving line.

Squatter Man gave that line a body.

That was the next major turn in the project, because it forced me to confront a problem that would later become central to the whole cosmology:

**one structure can look like different things from different viewpoints.**

Before that, comparison was still mostly object-based. A serpent looked like a serpent. A rod looked like a rod. A tree looked like a tree. A person looked like a person.

Squatter Man made that separation unstable.

The figure is recognisably anthropomorphic: a central body, lateral extensions, a pinched middle and an overall form that invites the eye to see a person.

But the same geometry can also be described without mentioning a human being at all.

It can be a central column.

A pinch.

Upper and lower lobes.

Transverse branches.

A luminous or structured axial phenomenon.

That ambiguity became one of the most productive ambiguities in Vardath Cosmology.

## Anthony Peratt and the figure in the plasma

Anthony Peratt became much more important to this project than a passing comparison with a few petroglyphs.

His work gave me a physical vocabulary for something I had already been circling around visually: a vast current can develop **recognisable shapes** as it pinches, filaments, twists and reorganises.

Peratt's plasma-physics work dealt directly with Birkeland currents, high-current plasma columns and Z-pinch behaviour. In a later series of papers he and his collaborators compared laboratory and simulated high-current plasma morphologies with ancient petroglyph forms. They described dozens of recurring forms and argued that some ancient images may have recorded an extreme auroral or plasma event. Later work reconstructed a proposed south-polar configuration containing pinched plasmoids and Birkeland-current filamentation.

That published work is the starting point.

My cosmology goes much farther.

I am not simply borrowing Peratt's proposed ancient aurora and placing it above the modern Earth.

I think the Squatter-Man form may be a **later, reduced appearance of something vastly older and larger**.

The figure in the sky may be a surviving echo of the same kind of current that helped form the world-system itself.

That possibility changed the scale of the entire cosmology.

### The Squatter Man as a current-state

The Squatter-Man form is important because it can be read as a sequence of plasma states rather than one frozen picture.

There is an axis.

There is a narrow central region.

There are wider structures above and below.

There are lateral forms that can become arm-like.

There are changing nodes, loops and filamentary features.

A person looking at that from the ground does not need to understand plasma physics.

The eye does what the eye always does.

It finds a body.

The column becomes a torso.

The lateral structures become arms.

Upper concentrations become head, horns or headdress.

Lower structures become legs or supports.

A dynamic electrical form becomes a giant person in the sky.

This is exactly the kind of transformation that Vardath projection grammar requires.

The event is physical.

The remembered image becomes biological.

The later myth becomes personal.

### Birkeland current rather than isolated lightning

The scale matters.

I do not picture the important current as ordinary lightning enlarged until it looks impressive.

A Birkeland-current system is more useful to my cosmology because it is filamentary, extended and capable of organising plasma along magnetic-field-aligned paths.

Peratt's wider plasma work is valuable here because it treats cosmic plasma as structured by currents, fields, double layers, pinches and filamentation rather than as featureless glowing gas.

That is much closer to the world-machine I am building.

The serpent is not one lightning bolt.

It is a **long-lived pathway**.

The world tree is not one flash.

It is the structure organised around that pathway.

The Squatter Man is not necessarily the current's only form.

It may be what one powerful pulse looks like from one particular place and phase.

### From Peratt's sky to my world-tree

This is where my extension begins.

I think the great current may run through the entire expanding set of worlds.

The worlds do not merely sit beside the current.

They may have **formed around it**.

The earliest pulse may have been enormous: not a local auroral disturbance, but a world-forming fire passing through a far less enclosed space.

Matter may have condensed, accumulated, fused or otherwise organised around that current.

What is now the physical enclosure of a world may partly be the cooled and settled residue of earlier current activity.

In that picture, the current comes first.

The enclosure grows around it.

The world tree is the long material history of the fire.

That is my cosmological extension, not Peratt's claim.

But Peratt gave me the missing physical image: a current does not have to remain an invisible line. Under the right conditions it can develop large, structured, repeatable morphologies.

### Why later pulses may be smaller

Once matter accumulates around the current, the next pulse does not travel through the same environment.

This is one of the ideas I now think may explain why the ancient Squatter-Man event could be immense to human witnesses while still being smaller than the primordial world-forming fire.

The first current moves through relatively open structure.

It forms matter and boundaries around itself.

That matter then becomes **load, shielding, resistance, enclosure and inertia** for later pulses.

Every successful world-forming episode changes the conditions encountered by the next one.

The current is still there.

But it has more world around it.

More material has to be heated.

More boundaries have to be crossed.

More of the pulse is absorbed, redirected or distributed through the lattice.

The later manifestation is therefore reduced.

Not harmless.

Reduced.

The current that may once have built the enclosure can later appear inside that enclosure as the Squatter Man.

This gives the cosmology a natural hierarchy of scale:

**primordial fire → world-forming current → enclosed later pulse → Squatter-Man / axial sky manifestation**

That hierarchy is now central to how I understand the Peratt material.

### Mount Meru as the reduced cosmic axis

Mount Meru fits naturally beside this.

I do not need Meru to be merely a stone mountain.

I also do not need the Squatter Man and Meru to be unrelated objects.

At the scale of a later enclosed world, a powerful axial pulse can create a vast central form in the sky.

From one angle it can look anthropomorphic.

From another it can look like a pillar.

At a larger landscape or cosmological scale it can be remembered as a mountain.

The same active region can therefore generate:

**Squatter Man as figure**

**Meru as mountain**

**rod as geometry**

**tree as living architecture**

**Birkeland current as moving physical pathway**

Those are not five things forced into one identity.

They are different descriptions of one axial event at different scales and viewpoints.

### The figure may be a diminished ancestor of creation

This is the part I find most important.

The Squatter Man may not be the original event.

It may be a **small descendant of creation**.

A later pulse re-enters the inherited pathways of the world-tree.

The accumulated material of previous ages limits and shapes it.

The current pinches.

The sky becomes structured.

A giant figure appears.

The axis becomes visible.

The world wakes.

The same family of process that once created the enclosure now temporarily reactivates inside it.

That would explain why the imagery feels simultaneously creative and catastrophic.

The current is both because it has always been both.

Its earliest work may have built.

Its later work may reset.

### Time remains open

I do not yet know how this part connects to time travel.

The cosmology increasingly treats previous, present and next worlds as neighbouring states that can become adjacent during the gate event.

The great current is clearly involved in creating the axial connection.

That makes it difficult for me to believe the current and the time-door are completely unrelated.

But I do not yet want to force the relationship.

Perhaps the current creates the geometry through which time-adjacency becomes possible.

Perhaps the world-turn structure already contains the temporal relationship and the pulse merely opens it.

Perhaps the primordial current built the physical world-tree while later pulses make selected parts of that tree traversable.

Those possibilities belong later in the book.

For now I leave the connection open.

What Peratt gave me here is more fundamental:

**the human figure in the sky can be the visible anatomy of a current.**

And once that is possible, the Squatter Man stops being an isolated curiosity.

It becomes a surviving image of the same fire that may run through the entire world-tree.

## The projection problem

Suppose a three-dimensional structure contains:

- a vertical axis;
- a narrow central pinch;
- wider upper and lower regions;
- paired lateral forms;
- bright local nodes;
- changing intensity over time.

How should a person draw it?

There is no neutral answer.

The observer has a position.

The event has a phase.

The drawing has a surface.

A three-dimensional and time-dependent object has to be compressed into a two-dimensional image or a narrative.

That compression is the beginning of what I now call **projection grammar**.

The same physical form can produce different symbols because the observer is not looking at the same projection.

Seen side-on, axial length dominates.

Seen end-on, length collapses and radial structure dominates.

Seen from below, an upper transverse structure can cross the vertical axis.

Seen during one phase, the form can be broad and branching.

Seen during another, it can be narrow and rod-like.

Seen in motion, the lobes and channels can become wings, limbs, serpents or many arms.

This was the first point where mythology began to look less like a list of unrelated images and more like a possible family of views.

## From body to axis

The most important change was conceptual.

I stopped asking whether Squatter Man was literally a man.

I started asking whether the **human form was a way of remembering the axis**.

That is a very different proposition.

A human body is one of the easiest frameworks for organising vertical geometry.

Head above.

Torso at centre.

Arms across.

Legs below.

If a phenomenon already contains a vertical spine and lateral structures, anthropomorphism does the rest.

This is not mysterious.

Humans see faces in clouds, figures in rock formations and animals in constellations. We are extremely good at turning ambiguous structure into bodies.

Vardath Cosmology does not require that ancient observers misunderstood a machine.

It requires only that an unusual form can be encoded through familiar biological shape.

That makes anthropomorphic mythology less of an obstacle.

A god-shaped image and a geometric structure do not have to be mutually exclusive descriptions.

One can be the humanised projection of the other.

## The hanging figure

Once the axial-human relation became important, hanging and suspended figures attracted attention.

A figure fixed to a tree.

A figure fixed to a cross.

A figure hanging from an axis.

A figure pierced by a spear.

A figure at the centre of a vertical and transverse geometry.

These are not historically one story.

Their cultural meanings are distinct.

But they created a strong structural family inside the Vardath model.

The important relation became:

> **conscious figure + central axis + transformation**

That formulation is much better than saying “all hanging gods are the same.”

It allows differences to matter.

### Odin

In *Hávamál*, Odin hangs on a windswept tree for nine nights, wounded by a spear, sacrificed to himself, before acquiring the runes.

The Norse religious and literary meaning is its own.

The Vardath comparison focuses on the geometry:

> **world tree / axis → figure fixed to centre → narrow penetrating rod → ordeal → hidden knowledge**

Odin is not merely standing near Yggdrasil.

His body is placed into the logic of the axis.

The result is a very dense visual and narrative configuration.

### Jesus and the cross

The crucifix is structurally different.

Its most useful Vardath feature is the explicit intersection of vertical and horizontal.

The body lies exactly at that crossing.

That makes the cross a natural image for:

> **axis × transverse plane**

The Christian meaning of crucifixion, resurrection and salvation remains Christian.

The Vardath layer comes afterward and asks why the form is so geometrically useful to the axis atlas.

### Buddha beneath the Bodhi tree

The Bodhi-tree comparison supplies an equally important contrast.

Siddhartha is not hanging from the tree.

He sits beneath it.

The central structure becomes a place of stabilisation and awakening rather than violent suspension.

This prevented the axis from becoming synonymous with catastrophe.

The Vardath relation becomes:

> **living axis + stable ground + conscious figure + transformation**

That is a quiet-axis state.

Odin gives ordeal.

The crucifix gives sacrifice at the crossing.

Buddha gives stillness beneath the living centre.

The commonality is structural; the transformation differs.

That difference becomes useful once the cosmology itself develops quiet and active phases.

## Tree, rod, pillar, staff

The axis atlas expanded from there.

A rod is the simplest abstraction of the axis.

A pillar is a structural rod.

A staff is a portable rod linked with an operator.

A tree is a living and branching rod.

A ladder is a narrow lattice strip that also functions as a route.

A mountain is an axis experienced at landscape scale.

A spear is a narrow penetrating axial form.

A sceptre is an axis translated into authority.

Once I saw those as roles rather than identities, many old comparisons became cleaner.

The model no longer had to claim that a sacred tree and a king's staff were historically the same symbol.

They could be different cultural uses of the same broad spatial category.

That is one of the most important methodological changes in the project:

**role before name.**

## Aaron's budding rod

Aaron's rod became interesting because it sits at the boundary between dead rod and living tree.

In Numbers 17 the rod buds, blossoms and bears almonds.

The Vardath comparison does not need to claim a physical cosmic object.

The structural transition is enough:

> **rod → living growth → sign of authority**

That maps elegantly onto the later model in which the narrow active axis and broad living tree can represent different states of one underlying structure.

The rod is not necessarily the tree cut down.

The tree can be the reopened, distributed form of the rod-state.

That interpretation only became possible after the finger-trap model, but the symbolic relationship was present much earlier.

## Meru and the mountain

Mount Meru entered the project because the axis does not have to look thin from every scale.

Near the surface, a vast convergence can look mountainous.

A central rise can have a broad base.

From far enough away or higher in the structure, the same object can narrow into a column.

From end-on, it can become a point or radial hub.

This is where the perspective problem becomes extremely powerful.

The mountain and the rod do not need to be separate mechanisms.

They can be scale-dependent views of the same axial region.

Again, this is a Vardath interpretation, not a claim about what Hindu, Buddhist or Jain traditions “really meant” by Meru.

The source traditions preserve Meru in their own cosmological systems.

My interest is in its role as an organising centre.

## Mashu and the traveller's gate

The Gilgamesh/Mashu branch added another viewpoint.

A gate does not always appear as something seen from below.

A traveller can approach it from the surface.

Mount Mashu, guarded passage and the extraordinary journey toward Utnapishtim gave the project what I came to call the **traveller's view of the gate**.

From below, an opening can look like heaven opening.

From the surface, it can become a mountain pass.

From inside, it can become a tunnel or dark route.

The object is not changing because the story is wrong.

The role is changing because the observer occupies a different relation to it.

That idea would later become central to the “many camera angles” framework.

## The eye at the end of the axis

Projection does not stop with side views.

Look down the axis.

The long form collapses.

Now radial structure matters.

A node can become:

- a ring;
- a wheel;
- a rosette;
- a star;
- a hub;
- an eye.

This became the end-on projection family.

The eye is particularly important because it introduces a second transformation:

geometry becomes agency.

A bright circular node overhead can be described as an eye.

An eye implies something that sees.

A node can become a Watcher in narrative.

That does not mean the Watchers of 1 Enoch are literally apertures.

It means the model now has a mechanism for how an aperture can be personified.

The chain is:

> **node → eye → watcher**

During a later active phase:

> **watcher / eye → opening → descending object or being**

This is speculative, but it is much more precise than merely saying “eyes are important symbols.”

## Wheels full of eyes

Ezekiel became especially interesting because the text combines radial machinery and eye imagery directly.

Wheels.

Wheels associated with wheels.

Rims.

Eyes.

Living beings.

Fire.

Radiance.

A vault.

A throne-like upper structure.

The Vardath comparison is not that Ezekiel saw the exact machine I describe.

The usefulness lies in role density.

A moving radial form and distributed eyes already coexist in the source imagery.

That is exactly the sort of relationship the projection grammar predicts if eye-like nodes belong to a larger moving lattice.

The source still belongs to prophetic literature.

The comparison belongs to my model.

## Side, end and broadside

By the time the projection grammar matured, I could organise the visual families into three major views.

### Broad or oblique

The weave dominates.

The form appears as:

- net;
- braid;
- knot;
- interlace;
- mesh;
- serpent field.

### Side or axial

Length dominates.

The form appears as:

- tree;
- rod;
- pillar;
- staff;
- mountain;
- ladder.

### End-on

Radial structure dominates.

The form appears as:

- eye;
- wheel;
- star;
- rosette;
- ring;
- hub.

These categories are not rigid.

The most interesting forms are transitional.

A mesh narrows into a ladder.

A ladder tightens into a rod.

A rod rotates toward the observer and becomes a wheel or eye.

A pair of winding channels broadens into a field.

A ring opens into a gate.

That is how the project stopped needing every symbol to be a separate object.

## The missing middle

The transitional images may be more important than the endpoints.

If the cosmology is correct on its own terms, the physical structure does not teleport from one symbol to another.

It changes continuously.

That means the model should generate mixed forms.

A rod with branching.

A ladder inside an enclosure.

An eye embedded in a mesh.

A wheel attached to an axis.

Serpents that form eye-shaped openings.

A tree whose branches become interlace.

A cross inside rings.

A central node surrounded by four or eight sectors.

These are exactly the kinds of compositions that became increasingly important as I looked across old imagery.

I do not expect every tradition to preserve a complete machine. Different cultures may preserve different views, different phases and different scales.

That is more useful to me than the idea that ancient art contains one uniform technical diagram.

## The human figure as projection

Squatter Man therefore changed the project in a way that goes far beyond one petroglyph category.

It introduced the idea that **anthropomorphism can be geometric**.

Once that is allowed, gods and giant figures can be reconsidered by role.

A radiant figure may be a manifestation associated with the axis.

A ruler may be an operator.

A many-limbed form may be a compressed human description of a complex surrounding structure.

A hanging figure may mark consciousness at the centre.

A giant may be a scale interpretation, an incoming being, or simply a later narrative personification.

Those are different hypotheses.

The model becomes better when they remain separate.

## Operator versus manifestation

This leads directly to the distinction that would dominate the next stage of the project:

**the figure is not necessarily the machine.**

A person can stand in front of an apparatus.

A rider can use a mount.

A god can command a vehicle.

A luminous form can magnify an operator.

A culture can remember the operator's identity and attach it to the entire event.

Once that distinction became explicit, comparative mythology stopped demanding impossible one-to-one equations.

Odin did not have to equal Yggdrasil.

Sleipnir did not have to equal the gate.

The gate did not have to equal the rod.

The rod did not have to equal the operator.

Roles could be distributed.

That is the point where the cosmology began to become a system.

## What Squatter Man really contributed

The lasting contribution of Squatter Man is not that a particular petroglyph proves a plasma catastrophe.

It is the **perspective problem**.

The same hidden structure can be:

- geometric in one view;
- anthropomorphic in another;
- radial in another;
- serpentine in another;
- architectural in another.

A culture does not have to preserve a blueprint.

It preserves what the structure looked like from where the witness stood, at the phase when the witness saw it, translated into the visual and narrative vocabulary available to that culture.

That idea became the bridge between physics and mythology inside Vardath Cosmology.

It also made the next question unavoidable.

If the figure belongs to an axis, what does the axis belong to?

That question produced the first world-machine.

---

# Chapter 3 — The First World-Machine

The early Vardath project had currents.

It had serpents.

It had a pinched humanlike axis.

It had trees, rods, mountains and hanging figures.

What it did not yet have was a world that could contain them.

That changed between December 2025 and February 2026.

The geometry became architectural.

For the first time, the separate symbolic pieces were placed inside one complete environment.

I think of this period as the construction of the **first world-machine**.

It was simpler than the current model.

As the project grew, several parts changed role, scale or relationship.

Almost every important component of the later cosmology was already there in some early form.

## The December enclosure

The December 2025 picture was essentially a room.

The inhabited world sat low inside a bell-like or tube-like enclosure.

Above it was a structured upper region.

Four elevated lands or sectors surrounded a central circular area or sea. Thin rivers divided the upper sectors. A central spike descended from the middle. A sphere or node hung below it. The outer rim continued downward into walls and a long tunnel.

The important feature was not only the arrangement.

It was the **viewpoint**.

The geometry was being imagined from below and inside.

That was a direct inheritance from the Squatter Man phase.

The observer did not have access to the blueprint.

The observer saw projections.

A fourfold upper arrangement could become a cross.

A central circular region could become a ring or eye.

A descending spike could become a rod.

A hanging node could become a star, jewel, head or sphere.

The enclosure was therefore already a machine built around the problem of perspective.

## Four around one

The fourfold upper structure survived much longer than many of the literal details.

Its simplest relation is:

> **four around one**

Four sectors around a centre.

Four rivers dividing the field.

Four supports around an axis.

Four directional powers around a central opening.

The cross is the simplest planar projection of that arrangement.

That does not make every cross a Vardath symbol.

It gives the model a reason why a fourfold shape can naturally appear when a vertical centre intersects a transverse field.

The later cosmology would expand from four directions to a denser lattice, but the old fourfold room was the first attempt to combine:

- a centre;
- a transverse field;
- flowing boundaries;
- a vertical connector.

That architecture would reappear repeatedly.

## The room becomes a body

By February 2026, the enclosure had become more than a room.

It became biological and cosmic at the same time.

The inhabited region remained below.

The upper zone was imagined as flooded, icy, vapour-rich or otherwise separated from ordinary life.

The central spike developed into a rod.

Two winding channels wrapped around that rod.

The structure became caduceus-like.

A living or crystalline cap was explored.

The whole enclosure began to feel less like a building and more like an organism.

This is where one of the deepest habits of Vardath Cosmology emerged:

**the machine and the living body are not necessarily opposites.**

The world-machine can grow.

It can carry currents.

It can form chambers.

It can have boundaries that behave like membranes.

It can enter active and dormant states.

It can generate environments in which later biology develops.

The current mature model still contains that ambiguity.

I often call the structure a machine because I am looking for repeatable geometry and mechanism.

I often call it living because it grows, persists, reorganises and generates environments.

The word *apparatus* may be the best compromise.

## The caduceus world

The paired channels were one of the most important additions.

They provided a way for the serpent intuition to enter architecture.

The world no longer contained one isolated current.

It contained a **central axis with winding paths around it**.

At the time, the open ends of the channels were explored as possible Sun and Moon positions.

Later, the Moon was explored as a possible projector of stars.

Planets were considered as plasma formations inside the enclosure.

I still keep those possibilities in the wider cosmology. I do not need to force one of them into the final answer yet. They can sit beside the later idea that the sky itself is part of the lattice structure and may have different behaviours in quiet and waking phases.

The geometry is what joins those possibilities together.

A central axis.

Two winding channels.

A larger enclosure around them.

A hidden upper region.

An inhabited lower region.

That is already remarkably close to the later braid, even though the mechanics were not yet worked out.

## The Sun, Moon and the open celestial branch

The early celestial interpretation remains one of the places where I prefer to keep several possibilities alive.

Two channels.

Two bright endpoints.

Sun and Moon.

The Moon as a possible projector or organising body.

Planets as material or energetic concentrations inside the larger enclosure.

Later, the sky itself became part of the lattice and the possibilities expanded again.

I do not need to choose between those pictures yet.

They may represent different states, different scales, different viewpoints, or pieces of the same larger celestial structure.

What matters for the book is that the sky belongs to the machine.

The Sun, Moon, planets and stars are not just decorative lights beyond the world in this cosmology. Their paths, appearances and relationships may be organised by the same larger structure that supports the world, wakes during the active phase and gathers toward the axis.

That lets the old caduceus picture remain useful.

Its endpoints may still matter.

Its paired channels may still matter.

Its relation to the rod may still matter.

Later chapters can explore how those pieces might connect to the breathing sky without forcing one interpretation to erase another.

## The cold upper region

The old enclosure also explored an extremely cold upper water or ice region.

A working temperature around −113 °C appeared in one branch.

I do not need that one value to define the whole upper region, but the branch opened a larger question that remains important:

**if water exists above the inhabited region, what state is it in and what supports it?**

A suspended or supported upper water immediately raises questions of:

- mass;
- pressure;
- phase;
- temperature;
- support;
- stability;
- energy.

The later model adds another possibility: the upper water may also be the lower watery boundary of the next world-turn.

That does not replace the older canopy image. It gives it another side.

The same region can be canopy from below, floor or lower boundary from above, and part of the lattice-dome structure that separates neighbouring worlds.

## Gravity, pressure and support

The enclosed-world picture also made me wonder whether what we call weight might involve more than one kind of support or directional force inside the world-machine.

That opened several possibilities:

outward pressure;

buoyancy-like effects;

changes in apparent weight with height;

local gravitational behaviour inside a larger lattice-supported world;

and interactions between ordinary weight, pressure and the deeper current.

I do not treat those possibilities as mutually exclusive.

The flat world-disc and lattice-dome picture makes the question even more interesting because support can operate at several levels at once.

The lived surface can have its familiar downward behaviour while the larger dome, boundary and world-tree structure may be held by different forces.

That means local gravity and larger lattice support do not have to be the same mechanism.

The branch remains open as part of the question of how a world-disc, its water, its atmosphere and its upper boundary are held in their quiet configuration.

## The early canopy

The flooded or vapour-rich upper region became the ancestor of the later **upper ocean** branch.

The older version imagined it mainly as part of our enclosure.

The newer version places it at the relation between world-turns.

That shift is worth following because it demonstrates how the whole cosmology matured.

Early question:

**How can a watery ceiling hang above our world?**

Later question:

**What if the upper watery boundary belongs structurally to an already populated neighbouring world?**

The second question does not magically solve the physics.

It changes the geometry of the problem.

The boundary can have two faces.

From our world it is above.

From the next turn it is below.

This introduced a habit of thought that became central to the physical model later: one structure can be described differently from opposite sides.

## The fourfold world becomes a field

The old four lands and four rivers also changed meaning.

In the early room, they were fairly literal features of the upper architecture.

In the mature model, fourfold organisation becomes one coarse view of a broader directional field.

The important relation is no longer that exactly four physical continents sit above us.

It is that a transverse surface can be divided around a centre, with flow boundaries between sectors.

Later, as the lattice becomes denser, this broad field can be understood as a higher-resolution directional weave rather than four literal upper lands.

The important thing that survived was not a preferred count. It was the relationship between **a spread field around a centre and a through-route along the centre**.

Four around one was the first crude picture of that relationship. The mature lattice keeps the same spatial intuition without making the book depend on number-pattern research.

## From room to shell-turn

The most important reinterpretation is scale.

The early enclosure felt like the whole world.

The mature cosmology treats one such stable region as a **turn inside a larger world-body**.

That single change absorbs many early components without requiring the old literal architecture to survive untouched.

The translation is approximately:

| Early enclosure | Mature Vardath interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| bell / room | one stabilised world-region inside a larger growing system |
| four upper lands | coarse transverse sectors / fourfold field |
| four rivers | flow boundaries between sectors |
| central spike | convergence axis / rod |
| paired plasma serpents | counter-wound braid strands |
| flooded upper region | boundary relation to neighbouring upper turn |
| canopy collapse | active boundary reorganisation |
| Sun/Moon tube ends | possible celestial endpoints or nodes within the larger sky structure |
| Moon projector | open celestial possibility within the wider sky branch |
| unusual gravity / pressure | open support branch alongside lattice-dome and local weight behaviour |

This is why I do not regard the enclosure phase as something left behind.

It is an **ancestor model** and still one view of the larger structure.

It supplied parts.

Later ideas connected those parts to more scales and more states.

## The apparatus emerges

The early enclosure also made it possible to separate **apparatus** from **operator**.

A room has architecture.

A vehicle has a driver.

A throne has an occupant.

A gate has a traveller.

A machine can persist when the person associated with it changes.

This seems obvious in ordinary life.

It was not obvious in the early mythology comparisons.

Without that distinction, every god or hero had to be the machine.

Once the enclosure existed, I could ask instead:

**Who is using the structure?**

That question transformed the comparative work.

A radiant god can be a manifestation or operator.

A mount can be a vehicle.

A serpent can be a channel.

A mountain can be the landscape expression of the axis.

A throne can be the authority position associated with the apparatus.

A witness can observe the event without controlling it.

The world-machine gave the cast somewhere to stand.

## One machine, many cultural faces

By August 2026, this became the explicit idea:

**one phenomenon, many gods**

I need to be precise about what I mean.

I do not mean all gods are secretly one historical person.

I do not mean every religion witnessed the same event directly.
